subject: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@northedge.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan

Hi Samir / Helen —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To make the on-site deployment run smoothly next month we need a short inventory + I/O profile from your infra team so we can finalize node sizing and the persistent volume strategy. At a minimum please send:

- Rack/uplink summary (top-of-rack switch models, available 10/25/40/100Gbps ports)
- Per-server CPU/GPU counts and exact NIC models
- Local disk layout (nvme vs. sata, capacity per device) and whether servers will expose local NVMe as ephemeral LVs or present them to k8s as local PersistentVolumes
- Expected steady-state concurrent replicas for inference (avg concurrent requests per model) and tail latency SLOs
- Any SAN/NAS present (NFS/SMB/iSCSI) and throughput/IOPS targets

Attachment: I attached a short Philips-style inventory template (site-rack-inventory.xlsx). If you prefer, send a CSV export and we’ll ingest it.

Goal: Deere (the deployment engineering team) needs final IO numbers by Mar 12 to lock the nodeclass CPU/GPU mix and whether we recommend local NVMe-backed PVCs or a shared block device.

Next steps: Can you confirm who on your side will own the NVMe carveout (ops or platform)? Also confirm if there are procurement lead times for additional NVMe drives — we may recommend we ship a small set of pre-provisioned NVMe sleds if procurement is slow.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@northedge.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan

Lauren / team —

Quick notes from my side based on the template and past site installs:

- For model-serving workloads we usually size nodes around expected concurrent requests per GPU rather than raw pod count. If NorthEdge expects 6-10 sustained concurrent generator sessions per rack, we should bias toward 8xA10/A100-equivalent GPU nodes or add a 10-20% burst pool.
- If they expose NVMe as local PVs we need an operator-level cleanup plan for pod eviction + secure wipe; otherwise we recommend LVM on top of NVMe and snapshots into the shared tier for checkpointing.
- Network: prioritize isolating control-plane egress (to redwood-control.redwood.svc) and ensure MTU 9000 if they want RDMA between NVMe pools; we'll add a kube-proxyless datapath option if they prefer minimal iptables overhead.

Attaching a small benchmark we ran last quarter (nvme-io-benchmark-2026.csv) — useful for setting IOPS per GB.

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@northedge.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Helen Park <helen.park@northedge.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan

Lauren / Dev —

Thanks — attaching the exported inventory CSV. Quick answers inline:

- Rack uplinks: two top-of-rack Mellanox SN2010 per rack, 100Gb active, spare QSFPs available.
- Servers: 2x dual-socket AMD Genoa, 8x NVMe per node (Samsung PM9A3), 2x 100Gb Mellanox ConnectX-6 NICs.
- NVMe will be provisioned by our platform team; ops will not reimage drives between tenants. We can expose NVMe as LVM-backed block devices to k8s.
- Expected steady-state: ~120 concurrent generator sessions across 12 racks (spiky). Tail P95 latency target is 200ms.
- SAN: none; we have an aging Isilon in DR only.

Notes: Procurement for additional NVMe (if needed) is about 4 weeks lead time. We are happy to coordinate a pre-shipment of sleds if that helps.

Samir
Samir Mehta
Head of Platform Engineering | NorthEdge Medical
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@northedge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan

Samir —

Great, that's exactly the level we needed. A couple of follow-ups from the ops checklist: 

1) NVMe carveout: if you present devices as LVM-backed block devices we will create a persistentvolumeclass with local topologies and a cleanup operator (secure-trim + DB tombstone) — please confirm whether nodes will be multi-tenant or dedicated to Redwood workloads.

2) Network: with ConnectX-6 and 100Gb uplinks we will recommend enabling jumbo frames and dedicate a VLAN for inference traffic to avoid noisy-neighbor pop-ins. We'll provide the VLAN ranges and MSLB plan once we lock the nodepool size.

3) Backups: since there's no SAN we should plan checkpoints to a remote S3-compatible object store; please confirm whether NorthEdge has an on-prem S3 gateway or whether we'll use a secure outbound link to your cloud bucket.

Action: Lauren and I will finalize a nodeclass proposal (GPU/CPU counts, NVMe PV class, PVC reclaim policy) and circulate by EOD Thursday (Mar 12).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Deployment Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@northedge.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: customer site deployment inventory and IO plan

Samir / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV. Attached is our preliminary nodeclass proposal and the preflight checklist (redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf). Key decisions we made:

- Nodeclasses: 8x A10-equivalent GPU nodes per rack with a 15% burst pool; dual-socket CPU for control-plane workloads only.
- Storage: NVMe presented as LVM-backed local PVs; PV reclaimPolicy=Delete with secure-trim hook on eviction. We'll also configure scheduled snapshot to your S3 gateway (please share access details).
- Network: MTU 9000, dedicated inference VLAN, and a kube-proxyless datapath for latency-sensitive pods.

Next concrete items for NorthEdge:
- Confirm on-prem S3 gateway endpoint and credentials (or confirm we can use secure egress to the cloud bucket).
- Confirm whether the NVMe carveout will be single-tenant or multi-tenant (affects wipe policy).
- Approve the nodeclass proposal by Mar 18 so we can lock procurement and deliver the sleds by Apr 20.

I will open a HubSpot task (linked) and a Confluence page for runbook ownership. If no major blockers we'll book a final tech-acceptance call for Mar 22.

Best —
Lauren
